introPt: A visitor discovers a long weekend the hard way, then learns the two questions.

dialogo.es: El lunes hacen puente, joven. Cerramos.
dialogo.pt: Monday is a long weekend — we are closed.

dialogo.es: Sí, y el martes muchos no abren tampoco.
dialogo.pt: Yes, and many do not open Tuesday either.
Are you going to be open?

opcoes: A holiday shifted to Monday to stretch the weekend
perguntas.explica: Several national rest days work exactly this way.

perguntas.pergunta: Is Semana Santa an official public holiday?
opcoes: No, but it is a huge travel week
perguntas.explica: Offices empty and beaches fill, with no legal holiday at all.

perguntas.pergunta: Which date is observed but not an obligatory rest day?
perguntas.explica: Widely observed; banks may close without being required to.

perguntas.pergunta: Why ask ¿ustedes van a abrir? after ¿es día festivo?
opcoes: Because small businesses decide for themselves
Because the first question is rude
perguntas.explica: Official closing and actual closing are different lists.

perguntas.pergunta: Someone describes their family Día de Muertos. What is the good move?
opcoes: Ask if an outsider may go
perguntas.explica: The question itself reads as respect, either answer is fine.
